blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Unit 3 (Integration), arranged by the unit's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation that shows the working.

blocks.prompt: 1 A function \(F\) is an antiderivative of \(f\) on an interval \(I\) when, for all \(x\) in \(I\):
blocks.explanation: By definition \(F\) is an antiderivative of \(f\) when \(F'(x) = f(x)\): differentiating \(F\) gives back \(f\).

book_ref.quote: A function \(F\) is called an antiderivative of a given function \(f\) on an interval \(I\)

blocks.prompt: 2 Which one of the following is an antiderivative of \(3x^{2} + 4\)?
blocks.explanation: \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^{3} + 4x + 7) = 3x^{2} + 4\). The constant 7 does not matter. The other derivatives are \(6\), \(3x^{2}\) and \(9x^{2} + 4\).

book_ref.quote: is also an antiderivative of \(f(x)\) on that interval

blocks.prompt: 3 The set (family) of all antiderivatives of \(f\) is called:
blocks.explanation: \(\int f(x)\,dx = F(x) + c\), the whole family of antiderivatives, is the indefinite integral of \(f(x)\).

book_ref.quote: is called the indefinite integral of \(f(x)\) with respect to \(x\)

blocks.prompt: 4 In \(\int (x^{2} + \cos x)\,dx\), the expression \(x^{2} + \cos x\) is called the:
blocks.explanation: The function written inside the integral sign is the integrand.

book_ref.quote: inside the integral sign is the integrand

blocks.explanation: \(dt\) shows the variable is \(t\), so the answer is in \(t\): \(5 \cdot \frac{t^{5}}{5} + c = t^{5} + c\). Without \(+c\) only one antiderivative is given.

book_ref.quote: It indicates the variable of integration
